newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch find second case of swine fever.
newsitem.headline: Dutch find second case of swine fever.

text.p: The Dutch Farm Ministry said on Thursday it had detected a second case of swine fever in the country and had closed off the farm involved.
But it said it had not yet decided on possible restrictions on the export of pigs.
"I can confirm that we have found a second case...an investigation is still going on," a ministry spokesman said.

The discovery follows the detection on Tuesday of the disease at a farm in the province of North Brabant, which resulted in one farm and two slaughterhouses being closed off. The second case was found in a pig from a farm a few miles away from the first.

The spokesman said around 1,700 pigs had been destroyed in the first case and 900 were involved in the second. He added that transport of all livestock within a 10 kilometre radius of the affected areas had been banned.
But it was still too early to say if there would be any restrictions imposed on exports, he said.

Germany earlier this week prohibited the export of pigs for slaughter from four German states after an outbreak of swine fever. Authorities have ordered the slaughter of over 14,000 pigs to contain it but Belgium and Switzerland have announced restrictions on German imports of live pigs and pork meat.
The U.S. Agriculture Department said on Wednesday it was monitoring the Dutch outbreak but would not impose any trade restrictions yet.
The Netherlands suffered its last outbreak of swine fever, which is highly contagious among livestock but is not dangerous to humans, in 1992.
